Ohne Zahl gibt es keine Aussage über Suchqualität. Der Harness ist das Werkzeug, das aus „fühlt sich besser an" ein „Hit Rate@5 steigt von 0,81 auf 0,87" macht.

Bewusst **ohne LLM**: Retrieval-Metriken sind reine Ranking-Metriken. Generationsmetriken (`RelevancyEvaluator`, `FactCheckingEvaluator`) folgen in einer späteren Phase und würden hier nur Laufzeit, Kosten und Rauschen einbringen.

Bewusst **nicht gegen ein laufendes System**: `QueryService` bündelt Suche und Antwortgenerierung, ein retrieval-only-Pfad existiert über die API nicht. Der Harness spricht `VectorStore.similaritySearch` direkt an und ist damit unabhängig von der Demo-Bereitstellung.

Spezifikation: `docs/features/search-quality-evaluation.md`, Abschnitt „Retrieval-Harness und Regression in CI". Metrikdefinitionen: `docs/discussions/discussion-rag-evaluation.md`, Abschnitt 2.1.

## Ziel / Ergebnis

Danach lässt sich die Retrieval-Qualität lokal mit einem Gradle-Aufruf messen und als Report ausgeben.

## Umfang

- Integrationstest im Backend, eigener Testtag/Task, damit er nicht Teil von `./gradlew build` ist
- Testcontainers: `pgvector/pgvector:pg18` und Ollama mit `nomic-embed-text` (Modellversion festgenagelt)
- Prüfung von `MANIFEST.sha256` vor dem Lauf; Abbruch bei Abweichung
- Indizierung des Korpus über die produktive Pipeline (`FileProcessingService` / `ChunkingService`), nicht über einen Sonderweg
- Abbildung der Treffer auf Entitäten über das Chunk-Metadatum `file_name`
- Metriken: Hit Rate@5, MRR, nDCG@10, Recall@10 — gesamt und aufgeschlüsselt nach Kategorie, Schwierigkeit und Sprache
- Report als maschinenlesbares JSON plus lesbare Zusammenfassung

## Außerhalb des Umfangs

- CI-Integration und Baseline-Vergleich (#228)
- Generationsmetriken, RAGAS-Sidecar
- Gepaarte Bootstrap-Vergleiche zwischen zwei Konfigurationen

## Abnahmekriterien

- [ ] Der Harness läuft lokal über einen eigenen Gradle-Task durch und erzeugt einen Report
- [ ] `./gradlew build` wird durch den Harness **nicht** verlangsamt (er ist ausgeschlossen)
- [ ] Ein manipuliertes Korpus-Byte führt zum Abbruch mit klarer Fehlermeldung (Manifest-Prüfung)
- [ ] Alle vier Metriken werden gesamt und je Kategorie, Schwierigkeit und Sprache ausgewiesen
- [ ] Der Report enthält die Konfiguration des Laufs: Embedding-Modell und -Version, `chunkSize`, `topK`, Ähnlichkeitsschwelle, Korpus-Manifest-Summe, Golden-Dataset-Version
- [ ] Zwei aufeinanderfolgende Läufe auf demselben Rechner liefern Metriken, die um weniger als 0,01 absolut voneinander abweichen (Nachweis der Stabilität; falls nicht erreichbar, ist die HNSW-Approximation als Ursache zu dokumentieren)
- [ ] Der Report weist die schlechtesten 10 Anfragen namentlich aus — der Harness soll Debugging ermöglichen, nicht nur eine Note vergeben
- [ ] Dokumentation aktualisiert: wie führt man ihn aus, wie liest man den Report

## Technische Hinweise

- Der pgvector-Indextyp ist in `application.yml` fest auf `hnsw` gesetzt (siehe #77). Approximative Suche kann Ranglisten leicht schwanken lassen. Falls das Stabilitätskriterium nicht erreichbar ist: Indextyp für die Evaluierung konfigurierbar machen oder exakte Suche verwenden — dann bitte im Issue vermerken.
- Chunk-Metadaten enthalten heute nur `document_id`, `chunk_index` und `file_name`. `file_name` ist deshalb der Schlüssel für die Zuordnung; die Dateinamen aus #225 sind eindeutig.
- Das Einbettungsmodell ist gemäß ADR-0008 Ollama, nicht OpenAI: kostenlos, ohne Secret, auch in Forks lauffähig und über die Modellversion reproduzierbar.

## Betroffene Module

`backend/` (Testquellen, Gradle-Build), `eval/`. Keine Änderung an der OpenAPI-Spezifikation, keine Änderung am Produktivcode erwartet.

## Abhängigkeiten

Blockiert durch #225 und #226.

## Teil des Epics

#224

opened_issues.title: feat(eval): Golden Dataset aus dem Frontmatter des Korpus ableiten
opened_issues.author: criew
opened_issues.body:
## Zusammenfassung

Aus dem YAML-Frontmatter des Comic-Korpus wird ein Golden Dataset abgeleitet: Frage-Vorlagen erzeugen Anfragen, die Ground Truth (Menge der relevanten Dokumente) ergibt sich rechnerisch aus den strukturierten Feldern.

## Kontext / Warum

Ein Golden Dataset ist der Schlüssel jeder Retrieval-Evaluierung (siehe `docs/discussions/discussion-rag-evaluation.md`, Abschnitt 5). Es von Hand zu schreiben skaliert nicht, und ein LLM raten zu lassen, welche Dokumente relevant sind, führt eine Fehlerquelle genau dort ein, wo Verlässlichkeit gebraucht wird.

Weil der Korpus aus strukturierten Feldern generiert wurde, ist die Antwort auf „welche Dokumente sind für diese Frage relevant?" eine Mengenoperation über das Frontmatter — exakt, nicht geschätzt.

Spezifikation: `docs/features/search-quality-evaluation.md`, Abschnitt „Golden Dataset".

## Ziel / Ergebnis

Danach existiert ein versioniertes Golden Dataset mit 100 kuratierten Fällen, gegen das ein Retrieval-Harness (#227) messen kann.

## Umfang

- Erweiterung des Werkzeugs aus #225 um einen Golden-Dataset-Generator
- Fünf Frage-Kategorien mit Vorlagen:

  | Kategorie | Vorlage | Ground Truth | Zielmetrik |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `attribute_lookup` | „Welche Augenfarbe hat {name}?" | genau eine Datei | Hit Rate, MRR |
  | `entity_description` | Paraphrase des Fließtexts | genau eine Datei | MRR, nDCG |
  | `multi_attribute_filter` | „Welche {alignment} Figuren von {creator} können {superpower}?" | alle passenden Dateien | Recall@k |
  | `numeric_range` | „Welche Figuren haben einen Intelligenzwert über {n}?" | alle passenden Dateien | Recall@k |
  | `crosslingual` | deutsche Frage auf englischem Korpus | wie oben | Robustheit des Embeddings |

- Ausgabe als `eval/golden/comic-characters.json`
- Manuelle Kuratierungsrunde über das generierte Rohmaterial

## Außerhalb des Umfangs

- Berechnung von Metriken (#227)
- Generationsmetriken und erwartete Antworttexte — dieses Dataset bewertet ausschließlich Retrieval
- Weitere Domänen (#234)

## Abnahmekriterien

- [ ] `eval/golden/comic-characters.json` enthält mindestens 100 Fälle
- [ ] Jeder Fall enthält `id`, `domain`, `query`, `expected_documents`, `category`, `difficulty`, `language`, `type`
- [ ] Alle fünf Kategorien sind mit mindestens 10 Fällen vertreten
- [ ] Mindestens 30 Fälle sind auf Deutsch bei englischem Korpus (`language: de`)
- [ ] Jeder Eintrag in `expected_documents` existiert nachweislich im Korpus (automatische Prüfung im Generator)
- [ ] Filterfragen haben eine Treffermenge zwischen 2 und 15 Dokumenten; darüber oder darunter werden verworfen
- [ ] Alle 100 Fälle wurden manuell durchgesehen: keine mehrdeutigen Fragen, keine Duplikate, keine Frage mit leerer Treffermenge
- [ ] Die Kuratierungsregeln sind dokumentiert, damit spätere Domänen denselben Maßstab anlegen
- [ ] Dokumentation aktualisiert

## Technische Hinweise

- Der Generator muss ebenfalls deterministisch sein (fixer Seed), damit ein erneuter Lauf keine neue Baseline erzwingt.
- Sinnvoll: eine Zusatzdatei mit den verworfenen Kandidaten und dem Verwerfungsgrund, als Nachweis der Kuratierung.

## Betroffene Module

`eval/`. Keine Änderung an `backend/`, `frontend/` oder der OpenAPI-Spezifikation.

## Abhängigkeiten

Blockiert durch #225 (Korpus muss existieren).

## Teil des Epics

#224

## Nachtrag zur Quelle

Der Korpus stammt aus `jrtec/Superheroes` (CC0-1.0) und umfasst rund 1.450 Entitäten, nicht 1.000 gesampelte. Die Zielgröße von 100 Golden-Fällen bleibt davon unberührt: Sie hängt am Fragenbedarf, nicht an der Korpusgröße, und liegt weiterhin am oberen Rand der in `discussion-rag-evaluation.md` §5.5 empfohlenen 50–100.

Der Attributreichtum der Quelle macht die Zielgröße sogar leichter erreichbar: sechs numerische Bewertungsfelder (`intelligence_score`, `strength_score`, `speed_score`, `durability_score`, `combat_score`, `overall_score`) speisen die `numeric_range`-Fragen, und rund 60 boolesche Fähigkeits-Merkmale lassen sich für `multi_attribute_filter` kombinieren, bis die Treffermenge im Fenster von 2–15 Dokumenten liegt.

opened_issues.title: feat(eval): Korpus-Generator für die Domäne Comichelden
opened_issues.author: criew
opened_issues.body:
## Zusammenfassung

Ein deterministischer Generator erzeugt aus einem eingefrorenen Snapshot des HuggingFace-Datensatzes `jrtec/Superheroes` (CC0-1.0) eine Markdown-Datei pro Comicfigur — mit YAML-Frontmatter (strukturierte Felder) und selbst formuliertem Fließtext.

## Kontext / Warum

Rohdateien sind für RAG unbrauchbar: Ein Datensatz mit tausenden Figuren ist für Tika ein einziges Dokument und wird vom `ChunkingService` an willkürlichen Zeilengrenzen zerschnitten. Zudem ist `.csv` gar kein unterstütztes Format — unterstützt sind `.md`, `.txt`, `.pdf`, `.docx`, `.pptx`.

Ein Dokument pro Entität löst beides: Bei `chunkSize=1000` Tokens und `minChunkSizeChars=350` ergibt ein Dokument von 1–2 KB genau **einen** Chunk. Ein gefundener Chunk entspricht damit eindeutig einer Entität — die Voraussetzung für saubere Retrieval-Metriken. Das Frontmatter ist zugleich die Ground Truth für das Golden Dataset (#226).

Spezifikation: `docs/features/search-quality-evaluation.md`, Abschnitt „Der Testkorpus". Entscheidung: ADR-0008 (Akzeptiert).

## Ziel / Ergebnis

Danach existiert ein reproduzierbarer, lizenzfreier Korpus im Repository, den sowohl der Regressionstest als auch die öffentliche Demo verwenden können.

## Umfang

- Python-Werkzeug unter `eval/generator/` (siehe ADR-0008: bewusst außerhalb des Gradle-Builds, läuft nie in CI und nie zur Laufzeit)
- Einmaliger Snapshot der Quelle, dokumentiert mit Quell-URL, Abrufdatum und SHA-256 der Rohdatei
- **Kein Sampling.** Der Datensatz umfasst rund 1.450 Entitäten (Splits `train` und `test` zusammen) und wird vollständig verwendet. Sortierung nach `id` vor der Generierung stabil festlegen.
- Ausgabe nach `eval/corpus/comic-characters/`, Dateiname als stabiler Slug mit ID, z. B. `comic-0142_spider-man.md`
- `MANIFEST.sha256` über alle generierten Dateien
- `SOURCE.md` mit Quelle, Lizenz (CC0-1.0) und Abrufdatum
- Kurze README zur Reproduktion des Laufs

## Außerhalb des Umfangs

- Golden Dataset (#226)
- Die weiteren drei Domänen (#234)
- Jede Änderung am Backend

## Abnahmekriterien

- [ ] Zwei Läufe des Generators mit identischem Input erzeugen byte-identische Ausgabe
- [ ] `eval/corpus/comic-characters/` enthält eine Datei je verwertbarer Entität (Größenordnung 1.400–1.450)
- [ ] Jedes Frontmatter enthält mindestens: `id`, `domain`, `name`, `real_name`, `creator`, `alignment`, `gender`, `type_race`, `place_of_birth`, `first_appearance`, `occupation`, `teams`, `eye_color`, `hair_color`, `height_cm`, `weight_kg`, die sechs Bewertungsfelder (`intelligence_score`, `strength_score`, `speed_score`, `durability_score`, `combat_score`, `overall_score`), die Liste der gesetzten Fähigkeiten, `source`, `license`
- [ ] Die rund 60 booleschen `has_*`-Merkmale werden als **Liste der gesetzten** Fähigkeiten abgebildet, nicht als 60 einzelne `false`-Zeilen — andernfalls dominiert Rauschen das Dokument und alle Entitäten ähneln sich im Vektorraum
- [ ] **`history_text` und `powers_text` werden nicht übernommen.** `history_text` reicht bis 130.000 Zeichen und würde die Zuordnung „ein Chunk = eine Entität" zerstören; zugleich bleibt so die Provenienz des Fließtexts eindeutig beim Generator
- [ ] Der Fließtext ist vom Generator aus den Faktenfeldern formuliert; **kein** Text wird aus der Quelle übernommen
- [ ] Kein generiertes Dokument überschreitet 4 KB (Nachweis, dass die Ein-Chunk-Eigenschaft hält)
- [ ] `MANIFEST.sha256` deckt alle generierten Dateien ab und lässt sich mit einem Standardwerkzeug prüfen
- [ ] `SOURCE.md` nennt Quelle, Lizenz und Abrufdatum
- [ ] Ein Zufallsmuster von 20 Dateien wurde manuell auf Lesbarkeit und faktische Übereinstimmung mit der Quelle geprüft
- [ ] Der Gesamtumfang des generierten Korpus liegt unter 5 MB
- [ ] Dokumentation aktualisiert (README des Generators, Verweis aus der Feature-Spezifikation)

## Technische Hinweise

- Quelle: https://huggingface.co/datasets/jrtec/Superheroes — 1.450 Zeilen, 46+ Spalten, **CC0-1.0**. Der Maintainer hat sich bewusst gegen den zuvor erwogenen FiveThirtyEight-Datensatz entschieden: CC0 macht Attributionspflicht und die Frage einer CC-BY-SA-Ansteckung über Fandom-Ursprungsdaten gegenstandslos. Ein Quellenhinweis wird trotzdem geführt, weil Nachvollziehbarkeit zum Charakter des Korpus gehört.
- Die Quelle ist für die Domäne ergiebiger als die ursprünglich geplante: sechs numerische Bewertungen und ~60 boolesche Fähigkeits-Merkmale liefern genau das Material für die Filter- und Bereichsfragen aus #226, an denen reine Vektorsuche scheitert.
- Tika liefert das Frontmatter als Teil des Fließtexts aus. Das ist gewollt (Attributbegriffe landen im Vektorraum), sollte aber bei der Formulierung der Fließtexte berücksichtigt werden.
- Datensätze ohne Namen oder mit leeren Pflichtfeldern werden verworfen; die Verwerfungsregel ist zu dokumentieren, damit die Dateianzahl reproduzierbar bleibt.
- Der Datensatz enthält eine `img`-Spalte mit Fremd-URLs. Sie wird nicht übernommen.

## Betroffene Module

`eval/` (neu). Keine Änderung an `backend/`, `frontend/` oder der OpenAPI-Spezifikation.

## Abhängigkeiten

Keine. Erstes Ticket des Epics.

## Teil des Epics

#224

opened_issues.title: Epic: Suchqualität messbar machen — Demo-Korpus und Retrieval-Regression
opened_issues.author: criew
opened_issues.body:
Suchqualität von OPAA bewertbar machen — mit einem lizenzsauberen, eingefrorenen Testkorpus, der gleichzeitig als öffentliche Demo dient. > **Korrekturhinweis (2026-08-02).** Zwei Aussagen dieses Epics waren falsch und sind berichtigt: > Die Instanz `opaa.ewerlin.com` läuft auf **OpenAI**, nicht auf Ollama mit `phi3:mini` — es besteht > also ein reales Kostenrisiko pro Anfrage. Und sie bleibt **account-gebunden hinter Keycloak**; ein > anonymer Lesezugriff wird nicht eingeführt. Die Ursache der ersten Fehlannahme war eine > Verwechslung des Anwendungs-Defaults in `application.yml` (`ollama`) mit der Compose-Belegung in > `.env.example` (`openai`). Beides ist in `docs/features/search-quality-evaluation.md` und im > Nachtrag zu ADR-0008 aufgearbeitet. ### Hintergrund OPAA kann heute nicht beziffern, ob eine Änderung an Chunking, Embedding-Modell, `top-k` oder Ähnlichkeitsschwelle das Retrieval verbessert oder verschlechtert. Jede Pipeline-Änderung ist ein Blindflug. Gleichzeitig fehlt ein vorführbarer Datenbestand: Interessenten sehen eine leere Installation. Beide Bedürfnisse teilen dieselbe teure Vorleistung — einen eingefrorenen Korpus mit bekannter Ground Truth. Deshalb werden sie gemeinsam umgesetzt. Die Metrik- und Framework-Theorie ist in [`docs/discussions/discussion-rag-evaluation.md`](../blob/main/docs/discussions/discussion-rag-evaluation.md) bereits vollständig geklärt (Golden Dataset, Hit Rate/MRR/nDCG, Spring-AI-Evaluatoren, Paired Bootstrap, RAGAS-Sidecar). Dieses Epic setzt deren Phasen 1 und 2 um und wiederholt sie nicht. Fachliche Leitentscheidung: **ein Dokument pro Entität, nicht die Rohdatei indizieren.** Eine CSV mit 5.000 Datensätzen ist für Tika ein einziges Dokument und wird an willkürlichen Zeilengrenzen zerschnitten. Stattdessen erzeugt ein Generator pro Datensatz eine Markdown-Datei mit YAML-Frontmatter plus Fließtext. Das Frontmatter ist zugleich die Ground Truth. **Spezifikation:** `docs/features/search-quality-evaluation.md` **Architekturentscheidung:** `docs/decisions/0008-search-quality-evaluation-harness.md` (Status: **Akzeptiert**) ### Befunde aus der Code-Prüfung Drei Annahmen aus der ursprünglichen Zielsetzung halten der Prüfung am Code nicht stand: 1. **Ein nginx-Container funktioniert nicht als Korpus-Server.** `AutoindexCrawlerService` parst Verzeichnislistings als HTML-**Tabelle**: `` mit mindestens vier `` und ein Icon-`` mit `alt`. Das Standard-`autoindex` von nginx erzeugt eine `
`-Liste und wird vollständig ignoriert. Der Demo-Webserver muss Apache httpd mit `IndexOptions FancyIndexing HTMLTable` sein.
2. **„Vier Domänen = vier Workspaces" ist heute nicht umsetzbar.** Dokumente tragen keine Workspace-Zuordnung, Chunk-Metadaten enthalten nur `document_id`, `chunk_index` und `file_name`, die Suche filtert nicht nach Workspace. Blockiert durch #115 und #117. Phase 1 und 2 bauen deshalb einen einzelnen gemeinsamen Index mit Domänentrennung über Dateinamen-Präfix.
3. **Es gibt kein E2E-Grundgerüst.** Kein Playwright, keine Browser-Tests. Das wird als eigenes Issue geführt.

Bestätigt hat sich dagegen: Der HTTP-Verzeichnis-Konnektor ist einsatzfähig, `.md` ist ein unterstütztes Format (`.csv` nicht), und ein Entitäts-Dokument von 1–2 KB ergibt bei `chunkSize=1000` Tokens genau **einen** Chunk — der Idealfall für saubere Ground Truth.

### Tickets

**Phase 1 — Comichelden end-to-end (Regression)**

- [x] #225 `feat(eval): Korpus-Generator für die Domäne Comichelden`
- [x] #226 `feat(eval): Golden Dataset aus dem Frontmatter des Korpus ableiten`
- [ ] #227 `test(eval): Retrieval-Metrik-Harness (Hit Rate, MRR, nDCG, Recall)`
- [ ] #228 `ci(eval): Retrieval-Regressionsjob mit Baseline und Schwellenwerten`

**Phase 2 — Demo (vorzeigbar)**

- [ ] #229 `feat(demo): Korpus als statisches HTTP-Verzeichnis im Compose-Stack`
- [x] #244 `docs: bestehende öffentliche Instanz opaa.ewerlin.com dokumentieren`
- [ ] #230 `feat(demo): Demo-Korpus auf die bestehende Instanz ausrollen`
- [x] #231 `test(e2e): Grundgerüst für browserbasierte End-to-End-Tests`
- [ ] #232 `test(e2e): Indizierung des Demo-Korpus über die Admin-Oberfläche`
- [ ] #233 `test(e2e): Suche im Demo-Korpus mit Quellenangaben`
- [ ] #250 `docs(security): Härtungsanforderungen für erreichbare Compose-Deployments dokumentieren`
- [ ] #252 `docs: Standardwerte in docs/deployment.md gegen application.yml abgleichen`

**Phase 3 — Ausweitung**

- [ ] #234 `feat(eval): Ausweitung des Korpus auf Filme, Reiseziele und Tiere`
- [ ] #235 `feat(demo): Demo-Domänen in getrennte Workspaces legen (blockiert)`

### Abhängigkeiten

```
225 ──┬── 226 ── 227 ── 228 ──────────────┐
      │                                   │
      ├── 229 ──┬── 230 ◄── 244           │
      │         ├── 232 ◄── 231           │
      │         └── 233 ◄── 231           │
      │                                   │
      └───────────────────────────────────┴── 234

#115, #117, 229, 234 ── 235   (blockiert; wartet auf das Workspace-Modell, nicht auf #198)
```

### Abnahmekriterien (Epic-Ebene)

- [ ] Ein deterministisch reproduzierbarer, lizenzsauberer Korpus liegt im Repository, abgesichert durch ein SHA-256-Manifest
- [ ] Ein Golden Dataset mit mindestens 100 kuratierten Fällen liegt versioniert im Repository
- [ ] CI meldet eine Retrieval-Regression automatisch, ohne dass ein Mensch danach sucht
- [ ] Der Korpus lässt sich über den bestehenden HTTP-Verzeichnis-Konnektor ohne neuen Ingestion-Code indizieren
- [ ] Eine öffentlich erreichbare, account-gebundene Instanz beantwortet Anfragen angemeldeter Nutzer an den Demo-Korpus mit belegten Quellenangaben
- [ ] Die laufenden Modellkosten der Demo sind gedeckelt: Ausgabenlimit beim Anbieter und wirksames Rate Limit pro Konto
- [ ] Der Quellenhinweis zum Korpus ist in der Demo sichtbar
- [x] ADR-0008 ist vom Maintainer entschieden (Akzeptiert)

### Außerhalb des Umfangs (eigene Epics)

- Generationsmetriken (`RelevancyEvaluator`, `FactCheckingEvaluator`) und der RAGAS-Python-Sidecar — Phase 4 der Diskussion
- Gepaarte Bootstrap-Vergleichsläufe für Konfigurations-A/B-Tests
- Ein eigener deutscher Benchmark aus Domänendaten
- Nutzer-Feedback-Kanal in der Demo als Quelle für echte Anfragen
- Workspace- bzw. Space-Modell selbst (#198)
- Wechsel des Chat-Modells der öffentlichen Instanz

### Referenzen

- `docs/discussions/discussion-rag-evaluation.md`
- `docs/features/search-quality-evaluation.md`
- `docs/decisions/0008-search-quality-evaluation-harness.md`
- Phase-1-Datenquelle: `jrtec/Superheroes` (CC0-1.0), https://huggingface.co/datasets/jrtec/Superheroes

---

### Entscheidungen des Maintainers (eingearbeitet)

| # | Entscheidung | Wirkung |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | ADR-0008 **akzeptiert** | Korpus im Repository mit SHA-256-Manifest, Python-Generator außerhalb des Builds, Java-nativer Harness ohne LLM, Ollama statt OpenAI in CI |
| 2 | Phase-1-Quelle ist **`jrtec/Superheroes` (CC0-1.0)** statt FiveThirtyEight | Attributionspflicht und CC-BY-SA-Ansteckungsfrage entfallen. Der Datensatz umfasst ~1.450 Entitäten und wird **vollständig** verwendet — Sampling und Sampling-Seed entfallen, was die Reproduzierbarkeit verbessert. Die Zielgröße von 100 Golden-Queries bleibt: Sie hängt am Fragenbedarf, nicht an der Korpusgröße. Die Freitextfelder `history_text` (bis 130.000 Zeichen) und `powers_text` werden nicht übernommen — sie würden die Zuordnung „ein Chunk = eine Entität" zerstören |
| 3 | **Ein gemeinsamer Index**, Domänentrennung über Dateinamen-Präfix | #235 bleibt blockiert und wartet auf #115/#117, **nicht** auf Epic #198 |
| 4 | Demo läuft auf der **bestehenden Instanz `opaa.ewerlin.com`**. Diese nutzt **OpenAI** — *korrigiert am 2026-08-02, siehe Korrekturhinweis oben* | Kein Hosting-Aufbau. Aber: Jede Demo-Anfrage kostet Geld, das Kostenrisiko ist real und wird über ein Ausgabenlimit beim Anbieter sowie Rate Limiting pro Konto begrenzt. #230 umfasst Rollout, Quellenhinweis, Kostenbegrenzung und Schutzmaßnahmen. Neu: #244, weil die Instanz bislang nirgends dokumentiert ist und #230 sonst nicht umsetzbar wäre |
| 6 | **Zugangsmodell der Demo:** account-gebunden hinter Keycloak, **kein** Gast- oder Read-only-Zugang. Dafür wird ausdrücklich **kein ADR** angelegt | Die Demo ist ohne eigene Installation nutzbar, aber nicht ohne Anmeldung. Der Zielkonflikt mit der ursprünglichen Begründung ist in der Spezifikation und in #230 offengelegt |
| 5 | **Korpus-Ablage** bleibt im Hauptrepository | Neubewertung als Prüfpunkt in #234 verankert |

opened_issues.title: feat: Anwendungstexte auf Deutsch umstellen (Frontend und Backend)
opened_issues.author: criew
opened_issues.body:
## Zusammenfassung

Die Benutzeroberfläche und die nutzerseitigen Backend-Antworten sind aktuell auf Englisch. Sie sollen auf Deutsch umgestellt werden, passend zur deutschen Projektsprache.

## Umfang

**Frontend** — alle sichtbaren Texte in `frontend/src` auf Deutsch:
- Seiten (`pages/`), Layouts (`layouts/`), Komponenten (`components/`)
- Platzhalter, Button-Beschriftungen, Fehlermeldungen, Snackbars, Tooltips
- `aria-label`-Attribute (Screenreader-Ausgabe ist Nutzertext)
- Datumsformatierung auf `de-DE` festlegen
- Zugehörige Tests, die auf Textinhalte matchen, mitziehen

**Backend** — nutzerseitige Texte auf Deutsch:
- API-Fehlermeldungen (`GlobalExceptionHandler`, Controller-Fehlerantworten)
- Default-Workspace-Name und -Beschreibung in `UserService`

## Nicht im Umfang

- Log-Meldungen, Exception-Messages für Entwickler und technische Konstanten bleiben Englisch
- Bezeichner, Dateinamen und Code-Kommentare bleiben Englisch
- Kein i18n-Framework — die Texte werden direkt auf Deutsch gesetzt

## Abnahmekriterien

- [ ] Keine englischen Texte mehr in der laufenden Anwendung sichtbar
- [ ] Frontend-Tests laufen grün
- [ ] Backend-Tests laufen grün
- [ ] Datumsangaben werden im deutschen Format ausgegeben

opened_issues.title: docs: Projektsprache Deutsch für Issues und Pull Requests festlegen
opened_issues.author: criew
opened_issues.body:
## Zusammenfassung

Die Issue- und PR-Templates sind bereits auf Deutsch, aber die Regelwerke schreiben weiterhin Englisch für Issue- und PR-Titel/-Beschreibungen vor. Dieser Widerspruch soll aufgelöst werden: Projektsprache für Issues, PRs und Dokumentation ist Deutsch. Ausschließlich der Quellcode (Bezeichner, Dateinamen, Commit-Scopes, Code-Kommentare) bleibt Englisch.

## Umfang

Folgende Stellen auf Deutsch umstellen:

- `AGENTS.md` — Regeln zu Issues und Pull Requests
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` — Hinweis zur Issue-Sprache
- `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/feature_request.md` — Hinweistext
- `.github/copilot-instructions.md` — falls betroffen
- `agents/roles/product-manager.md`, `agents/roles/developer.md`, `agents/roles/qa-engineer.md` — Sprachvorgaben für erzeugte Issues und Spezifikationen

Zusätzlich eine explizite Regel ergänzen, die die Sprachtrennung festhält.

## Abnahmekriterien

- [ ] Keine Datei schreibt mehr Englisch für Issues oder PRs vor
- [ ] Eine eindeutige Regel „Deutsch für Issues/PRs/Doku, Englisch für Quellcode" ist in `AGENTS.md` dokumentiert
- [ ] Agenten-Rollenbeschreibungen sind konsistent mit der neuen Regel

opened_issues.title: feat(agents): add six public-administration stakeholder agents for concept review
opened_issues.author: criew
opened_issues.body:
## Summary

The agent organization currently covers the delivery roles (product manager, developer, code reviewer, QA engineer, marketing). It has no role that represents the people who will actually have to live with the product inside a public authority.

This issue adds six stakeholder agents that review concepts and specifications from a named administrative perspective. They produce written assessments, not code.

## Roles

| Role | Perspective |
|---|---|
| `stakeholder-sachbearbeiter` | Caseworker. Daily routine work, low tolerance for extra steps. |
| `stakeholder-referatsleitung` | Unit head. Accountable for correct decisions made by their unit. |
| `stakeholder-ki-champion` | Technically capable driver of AI adoption inside the authority. |
| `stakeholder-betrieb` | Operations and IT security, runs the system and answers for it. |
| `stakeholder-skeptiker` | Persistent objector. Assumes every change makes things worse. |
| `stakeholder-personalrat` | Staff council. Co-determination, performance monitoring, data protection. |

## Scope

- Shared role contracts in `agents/roles/`
- Client adapters in `.claude/agents/`, `.codex/agents/`, `.opencode/agents/`
- `docs/AGENT-ORGANIZATION.md` extended with a stakeholder section and the roles table

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Six role contracts exist and state clearly that these agents never write production code
- [ ] Adapters exist for all three supported clients
- [ ] `docs/AGENT-ORGANIZATION.md` describes when stakeholder review runs and what it produces
- [ ] The assessment output format is defined and identical across the six roles

opened_issues.title: Governance controls for co-determination
opened_issues.author: criew
opened_issues.body:
## Context

Retention and governance controls for space-owned content. **The audit part moved to #239** and was
sharpened there: there is no person-based evaluation path at all, not even a switchable one.

Everything in this issue that once described a switchable per-person evaluation is **removed**. #239
is authoritative.

See [`docs/features/spaces-and-assets.md`](docs/features/spaces-and-assets.md) and [ADR-0008](docs/decisions/0008-space-and-asset-model.md). — section "Mitbestimmung und Personalvertretung".

## Scope

- Retention for chats, artifacts and **drafts**, presettable per space kind, with automatic deletion
- **Who sets the retention of a personal space:** the system admin, not the user — otherwise it never
  expires and growth is unbounded. Because this deletes work nobody else has ever seen, it only works
  with the two safeguards below
- **Advance warning before expiry, to the author**, so the export right can actually be exercised.
  Nobody clears a colleague's desk without notice
- **Extension option** for drafts on dormant matters — an objection, a court case or a deferred file
  is everyday administration
- A **"your open drafts" list for the author**, and only for the author
- Aggregation per organizational unit with a **stated minimum group size** and suppression below the
  threshold; the default is configurable, the floor is enforced
- **Storage capacity without an evaluation path:** occupancy reported only aggregated per
  organizational unit under the same minimum group size, plus a **technically enforced per-account
  quota** reported to the account holder themselves. A quota needs no evaluation path — the system
  enforces it and tells the person concerned
- No rankings, not even as a playful element
- Usage statistics fully switchable off without affecting functionality
- **Changes to governance settings are loggable and are displayed**
- External accounts are marked; adding them to a space with placed content requires explicit
  confirmation and is logged

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Chats, artifacts and drafts are deleted after the configured retention period
- [ ] The author is warned before a draft expires and can export or extend it
- [ ] The "open drafts" list is visible to the author and to nobody else
- [ ] **There is no draft counter, no "last active" indicator and no progress display** about another
      person's drafts
- [ ] Below the minimum group size an aggregate is suppressed rather than shown
- [ ] A per-account storage quota is enforced and reported only to the account holder
- [ ] Disabling statistics leaves search, chat and asset functions untouched
- [ ] A governance setting change produces an audit entry and a notification
- [ ] Backend format, build and test pass

## Depends on

#205, #206

## Note on the placement rate

Whether the placement model works can only be measured **aggregated per organizational unit above the
minimum group size** — never per person and never per space below the threshold. This is a
deliberately accepted price: measuring it precisely would break the assurance that makes the concept
defensible to the staff council.

Part of #198

opened_issues.title: Asset catalog: visibility, listed flag and space directory
opened_issues.author: criew
opened_issues.body:
## Context

Discoverability and non-visibility pull in opposite directions. A catalog entry reveals that
something exists. The `listed` flag makes that a deliberate decision instead of a side effect.

See [`docs/features/spaces-and-assets.md`](docs/features/spaces-and-assets.md) and [ADR-0008](docs/decisions/0008-space-and-asset-model.md).

## Scope

- `visibility`: `PRIVATE` | `SHARED` | `ORGANIZATION`; `listed` defaults to `false`
- Distribution levels realised through the grant subject: owner only, team group, department group
  (with curator approval, #208), whole organization
- Catalog search over assets the user may access plus assets explicitly listed
- Space directory honouring `PRIVATE` | `DISCOVERABLE` | `OPEN`, with request-to-join and one-click
  self-join
- Ownership may be a user or a group

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An unlisted asset never appears for a user without access
- [ ] A listed asset appears with description and responsible party, without granting access
- [ ] A grant to a department group gives every member access — the "department" distribution level
- [ ] Backend and frontend format, lint, build and test pass

## Depends on

#202, #200, #208, #209

## Note

Succession and orphaning moved to #240 and were substantially reworked there: account deactivation is
never blocked, assets move to "succession open" with frozen reach, a named curator and a deadline.

Part of #198

opened_issues.title: Built-in assets as a distinct origin type
opened_issues.author: criew
opened_issues.body:
## Context

OPAA ships proven public-administration agents and prompts. They must be updatable with the product
without ever overwriting what the authority changed.

See [`docs/features/spaces-and-assets.md`](docs/features/spaces-and-assets.md) and [ADR-0008](docs/decisions/0008-space-and-asset-model.md). — section "Mitgelieferte Assets".

## Scope

- `Asset.origin`: `BUILT_IN` | `LOCAL`
- Built-in assets have no user owner and are not editable in the authority
- Customization happens via a derivative, which is `LOCAL` and is never touched by updates
- An authority can **locally deactivate** a built-in asset it does not want to use
- **Update path for a network without internet access:** how product updates of built-in assets reach
  the authority, how they are signed and verified. Until this is answered, the specification must not
  claim built-in assets are simply "updated with product updates"
- Defined behaviour when no update arrives for a long time — in particular, no deadline mechanism may
  depend on a channel the authority does not have

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A product update never modifies a `LOCAL` asset
- [ ] A built-in asset cannot be edited in place; the UI offers "create derivative" instead
- [ ] A derivative of a built-in survives a product update unchanged
- [ ] A locally deactivated built-in stays present but unusable
- [ ] The offline update path is documented, or the claim of automatic updates is removed
- [ ] Backend format, build and test pass

## Depends on

#213, #212

Part of #198

opened_issues.title: Derivatives with permanent provenance and drift protection
opened_issues.author: criew
opened_issues.body:
## Context

Where parameters (#210) are not enough, a **derivative** is created. It carries its origin
permanently and is visibly marked as derived. There is no silent copying.

This issue contains only the two cheap and immediately useful parts. **Deadlines, review requests and
automatic deactivation are deferred to #243** — that is the most complex behaviour in the model and
the only place where an asset changes state without action by its owner. It presupposes that
derivatives arise in relevant numbers, which #210 is meant to prevent.

See [`docs/features/spaces-and-assets.md`](docs/features/spaces-and-assets.md) and [ADR-0008](docs/decisions/0008-space-and-asset-model.md). — sections "Abkömmlinge (Forks)" and "Das Abdriften von Abkömmlingen".

## Scope

- Create a derivative from any accessible asset; it records source asset and source version
  permanently
- Visible "derived from" marking in catalog, detail view and at point of use
- Version drift indicator: "based on version 3 — the original is at version 5"
- Notification of the responsible party on a new original version; with group ownership the
  notification goes to the unit
- Change view of what happened in the original. **No automatic merge** — not planned, and the UI must
  not suggest it

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A derivative always resolves to its source asset and source version
- [ ] The derived marking cannot be removed
- [ ] A new version of the original raises the drift indicator and notifies the responsible party
- [ ] Backend and frontend format, lint, build and test pass

## Depends on

#211

Part of #198

opened_issues.title: Recall by deactivation, with warnings in existing transcripts
opened_issues.author: criew
opened_issues.body:
## Context

An asset that is factually outdated is **deactivated, never deleted**. Decisions may have been
issued on the basis of earlier answers, so the trail has to survive for audits and appeals.

See [`docs/features/spaces-and-assets.md`](docs/features/spaces-and-assets.md) and [ADR-0008](docs/decisions/0008-space-and-asset-model.md). — section "Rückruf durch Deaktivieren".

## Scope

- `Asset.status`: `ACTIVE` | `DEACTIVATED`
- Deactivation requires a **stated reason** — without it the warning is noise and gets ignored
- A deactivated asset is not invocable and disappears from the catalog
- Existing chats stay fully readable and carry a visible warning **at the messages where the asset
  was used**, showing reason and date
- A deactivated knowledge library returns no hits; existing citations remain readable and their
  deep links stay permission-checked

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Deactivation without a reason is rejected
- [ ] A deactivated asset cannot be invoked and is absent from the catalog
- [ ] Existing transcripts remain complete and readable
- [ ] The warning appears at the messages that actually used the asset, not on the whole chat
- [ ] Nothing is deleted anywhere in this flow
- [ ] Backend and frontend format, lint, build and test pass

## Depends on

Provenance tracking (#204), persistent chats (#205)

Part of #198

opened_issues.title: Asset versioning with immediate propagation and rollback
opened_issues.author: criew
opened_issues.body:
## Context

A distributed asset is a **reference**, not a copy: everyone works with the same object, so an
improvement takes effect for all users on their next invocation. That is only acceptable with a
complete history and a way back.

See [`docs/features/spaces-and-assets.md`](docs/features/spaces-and-assets.md) and [ADR-0008](docs/decisions/0008-space-and-asset-model.md). — section "Verteilung von Assets".

## Scope

- `AssetVersion` with author, timestamp, reason and a snapshot of the configuration
- Active version pointer on the asset; changes take effect immediately for all users
- Rollback by activating an earlier version, recorded as its own event — intermediate versions are
  never deleted
- Version comparison view

**Versioned is the configuration**, not the document holdings: for an agent the task description,
bound libraries, model choice and parameters; for a prompt library its prompts; for a knowledge
library its configuration. Document versioning is a separate topic and explicitly not in scope.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every change to an asset configuration produces a version with author, time and reason
- [ ] After a change, the next invocation by any user uses the new version
- [ ] Rolling back activates an earlier version without deleting anything
- [ ] The history shows what changed between two versions
- [ ] Backend and frontend format, lint, build and test pass

## Depends on

Agent and prompt library assets (#209)

Part of #198

opened_issues.title: Asset parameters: adapt without forking
opened_issues.author: criew
opened_issues.body:
## Context

The most common reason to fork an agent is trivial — a different register, an extra note. Forking
for that reason severs the maintenance link to the original, which is exactly what must be avoided.

**Sequencing matters:** this ships **together with** agent sharing, not after it. Forks created in
the meantime cannot be collected back in.

See [`docs/features/spaces-and-assets.md`](docs/features/spaces-and-assets.md) and [ADR-0008](docs/decisions/0008-space-and-asset-model.md). — section "Anpassen ohne Fork: Parameter".

## Scope

- The asset owner declares a short, **typed** parameter list: name, type, allowed values, default
- Recipients set values per user, group or space without forking
- Parameter values are applied at invocation time

Deliberately **not** a templating system: no loops, no conditionals, no free text substitution in
the system prompt. A short typed list, nothing more.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An owner can declare parameters with allowed values and defaults
- [ ] A recipient can set values without creating a derivative
- [ ] A value outside the allowed set is rejected
- [ ] Changing a parameter value does not create an asset version — it is usage configuration,
      not a change to the asset
- [ ] Improvements to the original still reach users who set parameter values
- [ ] Backend and frontend format, lint, build and test pass

## Depends on

Agent and prompt library assets (#209) — ship in the same release

Part of #198

opened_issues.title: Agent and prompt library assets with the knowledge share chain
opened_issues.author: criew
opened_issues.body:
## Context

The second and third asset types. They inherit the permission and association model unchanged; what
is new is the **share chain**, which is how a shared agent actually works for the recipient.

An agent always retrieves with the **rights of the calling user**. There is no mode in which it reads
with its own rights.

See [`docs/features/spaces-and-assets.md`](docs/features/spaces-and-assets.md) and [ADR-0008](docs/decisions/0008-space-and-asset-model.md).

## Scope

- `Agent` asset: task description, explicitly bound knowledge libraries, model choice
- `PromptLibrary` asset
- Share chain when sharing an agent:
  1. show which libraries the agent needs and whether the recipient already has access
  2. request co-release from each missing library's owner
  3. each owner approves or declines — a co-release is just an additional grant
  4. report the result, e.g. "2 of 3 co-released, the agent will work with reduced scope"
- The `USER` role lets someone run an agent without seeing its configuration

### Non-response, not refusal, is the normal case

- [ ] Every request has a **deadline**; on expiry it escalates to the curator of the library owner's
      organizational unit
- [ ] The waiting state is visible to both sides ("waiting 6 days on Referat 34")
- [ ] **The recipient sees on the agent itself** that a knowledge source is missing — not only in
      worse answers. Otherwise they conclude the agent is useless instead of realising a release is
      pending
- [ ] The library owner is shown **at the moment of their decision** that a co-release means read
      access to the entire raw material, not only to what the agent actually uses

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Sharing lists required libraries and the recipient's current access
- [ ] A co-release creates a normal grant and is audited
- [ ] A declined co-release still shares the agent, with reduced scope shown to both sides
- [ ] An unanswered request escalates after the deadline
- [ ] A user with `USER` on an agent can run it but cannot see its task description, bound libraries
      or document lists
- [ ] An agent behaves identically regardless of the space it runs in
- [ ] No code path retrieves with anything other than the calling user's rights
- [ ] Backend and frontend format, lint, build and test pass

## Depends on

#202, #203

## Deliberate omission

An agent whose knowledge may not be co-released is **not shareable**. Shared agents work reliably
only where the chain completes — this must not be omitted when presenting the product.

Part of #198

opened_issues.title: Curator roles bound to organizational units
opened_issues.author: criew
opened_issues.body:
## Context

Distribution levels map onto the organizational structure the authority already maintains in its
directory, not onto a space hierarchy. Releasing an asset to a unit requires that unit's curator.

Curator staffing is **optional and grows with the organization**: a pilot authority names a single
central curator and is immediately operational.

See [`docs/features/spaces-and-assets.md`](docs/features/spaces-and-assets.md) and [ADR-0008](docs/decisions/0008-space-and-asset-model.md). — section "Verteilung von Assets".

## Scope

- Curator assignment per organizational unit (a user or a group)
- Resolution with **upward fallback**: no curator on a unit means the next higher unit's curator is
  responsible, ultimately the organization curator
- Release to an org unit requires curator approval
- Curators are not owners — curation and ownership stay separate

### Closing the reach loophole

Without a rule there is an open path around curation: whoever cannot get a release to "Abteilung 5"
approved creates an `AD_HOC` group with the same people — materially the same reach, formally no
release to the unit.

- [ ] A grant to a group **above a configurable size** requires curator approval, **regardless of
      group kind**. For ad-hoc groups the curator of the granting person's unit is responsible
- [ ] The threshold is evaluated on the **cumulative reach per asset and grantee set**, not per
      individual grant — otherwise a release to 40 people is split into two grants of 20
- [ ] A group that **grows past the threshold** through directory synchronisation flags the existing
      grant for curator review. The grant is not revoked automatically, but it does not silently
      keep a reach it was never approved for
- [ ] Small ad-hoc groups — the ordinary project circle — stay free of curation
- [ ] **Open requests with dwell time appear on a list** and the dwell time is measurable

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A release to a unit without its own curator routes to the next higher unit
- [ ] With a single organization-level curator, every request reaches that person
- [ ] Approving creates a normal grant to the unit group and is audited
- [ ] Splitting a release into several grants does not evade the threshold
- [ ] A group growing past the threshold flags its grants for review
- [ ] A curator gains no ownership rights over the assets they approve
- [ ] Backend format, build and test pass

## Depends on

#200

## Note

The curator role must be named **and funded with working time**. That is an introduction question,
not a technical one; the product only makes dwell times visible.

Part of #198

opened_issues.title: Connector sources target exactly one knowledge library
opened_issues.author: criew
opened_issues.body:
## Context

A connector source used to map to one or more workspaces, multiplying chunks. It now feeds exactly
one knowledge library.

See [`docs/features/spaces-and-assets.md`](docs/features/spaces-and-assets.md) and [ADR-0008](docs/decisions/0008-space-and-asset-model.md).

## Scope

- `SourceMapping.targetLibrary`, single-valued
- Exclusion of individual connector documents, acting on the library
- System admin decides where indexing goes; the library owner decides who sees it

### The release cap must be defined, not just mentioned

It is the only technical safeguard between "specialist-system data ingested" and "readable
organization-wide", and it currently appears in several documents without a definition. It now also
carries more weight, because lowering it triggers "precondition violated" in strict spaces (#204).

- [ ] Defined **what** is capped: `visibility`, `listed`, and grants to groups above a given size
- [ ] Defined what happens when it is **lowered afterwards** — are existing wider grants withdrawn or
      only new ones prevented. For an auditor this is the difference between "fixed" and "not fixed"
- [ ] Defined whether a library fed from a connector **and** manual upload carries the cap

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A source maps to exactly one library; multi-target mappings are rejected
- [ ] A library owner cannot raise visibility beyond the cap
- [ ] Lowering the cap behaves as defined and is logged
- [ ] An excluded document is removed from the index and skipped on subsequent runs
- [ ] Backend format, build and test pass

## Depends on

#201

Part of #198

opened_issues.title: Artifacts in spaces with lifecycle and provenance-based release
opened_issues.author: criew
opened_issues.body:
## Context

Results created in a space — spreadsheets, charts, later reports and drafts — follow **the same rule
as chats**: draft belonging to the creator, visible by placing. The earlier provenance-dependent
special case is dropped: a result was sometimes immediately visible and sometimes not, without the
creator being able to explain the difference — they do not know the reader circles of the libraries
involved.

See [`docs/features/spaces-and-assets.md`](docs/features/spaces-and-assets.md) and [ADR-0008](docs/decisions/0008-space-and-asset-model.md).

## Scope

- A generic space-owned content type so further result types can be added without a model change
- `Artifact`: origin chat, name, content type, storage reference, provenance, status
- Uniform status `DRAFT` -> `PLACED` -> `SUPERSEDED` | `WITHDRAWN`, plus `replaces` for versioning
- Visible provenance label, traceable back to the origin chat
- **Withdraw instead of delete**, logged with a reason
- Retention per space; **drafts are subject to it as well**
- Promote an artifact into a knowledge library: it becomes a document and **from then on the
  library's permissions apply, not the space's**

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every artifact behaves identically regardless of the origin of its data
- [ ] A draft is visible only to its creator
- [ ] Placing is one click, with the same dialog and hint as for chats
- [ ] Superseded artifacts remain findable
- [ ] Neither creator nor space admin can erase an artifact; both can withdraw it
- [ ] Promoting an artifact into a library switches the governing permissions
- [ ] Backend and frontend format, lint, build and test pass

## Depends on

#205

Part of #198

opened_issues.title: Persistent chats inside spaces
opened_issues.author: criew
opened_issues.body:
## Context

**This is new construction, not a rename.** Today only `CaffeineChatMemoryRepository` exists —
in-memory chat memory plus a validated `conversationId` string.

A chat is a persistent object inside exactly one space. It is created as a **draft belonging to its
author** and becomes visible to all space members when the author **places** it. The earlier promise
"every member sees every chat" is revoked.

This creates the thinking space before placement: the unfinished assessment, the difficult personnel
matter, the question asked three times out of uncertainty. Nobody has to switch spaces or fall back
to email for that.

See [`docs/features/spaces-and-assets.md`](docs/features/spaces-and-assets.md) and [ADR-0008](docs/decisions/0008-space-and-asset-model.md).

## Scope

- `Chat` (space-owned): title, space, author, organization, optional bound agent, status
- Status `DRAFT` -> `PLACED` -> `WITHDRAWN`
- `ChatMessage`: author (user or agent), role, content, citations, timestamp
- Reserve the axes for later human+AI group rooms: `ChatParticipant` with `READER` | `WRITER`,
  `parentMessageId` for threads, mentions
- **Provenance tracking** (moved here from #204): every chat records which libraries actually
  contributed hits. The placement dialog hint depends on it, so it cannot come later
- Chatting requires space membership; joining an `OPEN` space is one click and is audited
- Search scope: space associations for an unbound chat, the agent's bound libraries for a bound one.
  **In the personal space the scope is everything the user may read** — there is nothing to curate in
  a one-person room, and without this the fallback would only be formal
- UI: the chat permanently shows its status and, once placed, who can read along

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Chats and messages survive a restart
- [ ] A chat belongs to exactly one space and cannot be moved out of it
- [ ] A draft is visible **only** to its author — not to space admins, not to system admins
- [ ] Placing is **one click** and is not hidden behind a menu
- [ ] The reader circle is named before the placement takes effect
- [ ] If the chat used libraries not all members may read, that appears **as a hint inside the
      placement dialog** — with the **name of the library owner**, without counts and without
      library names. The owner name is not a secret like the content, and without it the placing
      person cannot judge whether passing it on is acceptable
- [ ] The author can withdraw a placed chat
- [ ] **A space admin can withdraw a placed chat but not erase it**; the removal is logged with a
      reason
- [ ] The author can export a chat at any time, **including drafts**
- [ ] **The author is notified when the reader circle of their placed content materially expands** —
      new members, external persons, a space being opened — so that the withdrawal option is usable
- [ ] Backend and frontend format, lint, build and test pass

## Depends on

#203

## Note

The cost is stated explicitly: automatic transparency is traded for voluntary transparency. A chat
nobody places does not exist for the organization.

Part of #198

opened_issues.title: Strict mode for spaces
opened_issues.author: criew
opened_issues.body:
## Context

Strict mode is the only place where the model offers a **technical assurance** instead of a
responsible human act. It is off by default and recommended for audit, internal review and HR
spaces.

An earlier version promised "guaranteed leak-free" and could not deliver, because a space does not
narrow an agent's search scope.

See [`docs/features/spaces-and-assets.md`](docs/features/spaces-and-assets.md) and [ADR-0008](docs/decisions/0008-space-and-asset-model.md). — section "Der Strikt-Modus".

## Scope

- `Space.strictKnowledge`, off by default, settable by system admin or space owner
- Only libraries whose reader circle covers **all** members may be associated
- **An agent whose bound libraries are not all in that set cannot be invoked in the space.** The
  resolution is neither to narrow the agent (that would break reproducibility) nor to withdraw the
  assurance, but to **refuse the invocation**: the agent runs with its complete binding or not at
  all. The user gets a clear message
- **Strict-only libraries propagate to bindings:** a library marked strict-only can only be bound by
  agents that are themselves invocable only in strict spaces. Without this the marking would guard
  the association — which this model declares harmless — while leaving the agent path open
- **Membership additions that would break the precondition are refused at the door**, naming which
  grant is missing. This is the only trigger the acting person controls and sees in advance;
  otherwise a space admin locks his own room for twelve people without warning

### When the precondition breaks afterwards

Triggers: directory synchronisation, grant withdrawal, a lowered release cap. The space enters the
state **"precondition violated"**:

- [ ] Existing content stays untouched and readable
- [ ] **New placements and agent invocations are blocked** until resolved
- [ ] **Named addressee, deadline and escalation** — as with "succession open" (#240): the state
      appears on the list of the curator of the library owner's organizational unit, with a deadline
      and escalation upward. Not merely "the responsible parties are notified"
- [ ] The **system admin gets a list with dwell time**, like open curator requests
- [ ] **Re-evaluation is triggered by every rights change on every library associated in any strict
      space.** Without this the state does not clear itself when the cause disappears
- [ ] The cause goes to the space owner **in plain text**: which library, which event, which time
- [ ] The user-facing message identifies the state as a **business condition, not a malfunction**,
      and names who is responsible
- [ ] The state change is explicitly **not an on-call event**, documented as such — otherwise
      someone resets a membership at night to "fix the outage"

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] In a strict space, associating a narrower library is rejected
- [ ] An agent with insufficiently covered bindings cannot be invoked and the user is told why
- [ ] A strict-only library cannot be bound by an agent invocable outside strict spaces
- [ ] A membership addition that would break the precondition is refused with the missing grant named
- [ ] A broken precondition blocks placements and invocations, destroys nothing, and appears on a
      curator list with a deadline
- [ ] A rights change on any library restores the state automatically when the cause disappears
- [ ] Backend and frontend format, lint, build and test pass

## Depends on

#205 (placement), #209 (agents)

## Note

Provenance tracking moved to #205 — the placement dialog needs it, and #205 comes first.

Part of #198

opened_issues.title: Space-asset association as pure curation
opened_issues.author: criew
opened_issues.body:
## Context

An association makes an asset available in a space. It grants **nothing** — and under the placement
model it exposes nobody either, because content only becomes visible when its author places it.

See [`docs/features/spaces-and-assets.md`](docs/features/spaces-and-assets.md) and [ADR-0008](docs/decisions/0008-space-and-asset-model.md).

## Scope

- `SpaceAssetAssociation`: space, asset, createdBy, createdAt
- A curator may associate any asset they themselves have access to. **No curator confirmation for
  mixed audiences** and **no permanent mixed-space marking** — both were dropped: the association
  exposes nobody, and a warning sign attached to nearly every space informs about nothing
- The asset owner sees all associations and may detach any of them unilaterally
- **The owner is actively notified** when their library is made available in a space whose members
  do not all have read access. No consent required, but they learn of it without having to check a
  list
- **Owner self-protection:** a library owner can mark a library as usable **only in strict spaces**.
  The marking propagates to bindings — see #204
- Switching a library to strict-only while it is already associated in non-strict spaces is only
  possible after the owner resolves the conflict: the system lists the conflicting associations and
  the owner detaches them or aborts. No silent background change
- Space view lists associated assets **filtered to what the viewing user may access**
- Search scope for a chat without a bound agent: associated libraries of the space intersected with
  the user's readable libraries

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Associating an asset changes no user's effective permissions — explicit test
- [ ] Two members of the same space with different grants see different asset lists
- [ ] The asset owner can detach an association created by someone else
- [ ] The owner is notified when their library lands in a space with a narrower reader circle
- [ ] Switching to strict-only lists conflicting associations and requires an explicit decision
- [ ] Deleting a space removes associations but leaves the assets untouched
- [ ] The UI explains once, visibly, why the asset list differs per member
- [ ] Backend and frontend format, lint, build and test pass

## Depends on

#202

Part of #198

opened_issues.title: Asset permissions and permission-aware vector search
opened_issues.author: criew
opened_issues.body:
## Context

The central gap of the current implementation: `QueryService` performs a similarity search with no
metadata filter whatsoever. Until this issue is done, the whole model is a facade.

See [`docs/features/spaces-and-assets.md`](docs/features/spaces-and-assets.md) and [ADR-0008](docs/decisions/0008-space-and-asset-model.md).

## Scope

- `AssetGrant`: subject (user or group) -> role `USER` | `VIEWER` | `EDITOR` | `MANAGER` | `OWNER`,
  a rank order **separate** from the space roles
- **The managing asset role is `MANAGER`, not `ADMIN`** — no role name occurs in both role systems.
  Whoever says "admin rights" always means a space
- **Every grant carries an optional expiry field from the start**, even though recertification only
  arrives with #241. Adding the field later is cheap; assessing an existing body of grants without
  one is not
- Resolution of `readableLibraries(user)` = direct grants + group grants + organization-wide
  libraries. **Space associations do not appear in this expression**
- Caching with immediate invalidation on any permission change
- Metadata filter on `library_id` inside `VectorStore.similaritySearch` — part of the search, not a
  post-filter
- The retrieval context is always the calling user; there is no second rights context

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A user only receives chunks from libraries they may read; verified against a library they have
      no grant on
- [ ] Revoking a grant takes effect on the next query
- [ ] Space membership alone grants no access to any library — explicit negative test
- [ ] Group grants work identically to direct grants
- [ ] No role name exists simultaneously in `SpaceRole` and the asset role enum
- [ ] An empty readable set produces an empty result, not an error, and the message reveals no counts
- [ ] Permission resolution adds less than 50 ms to query time
- [ ] Backend format, build and test pass

## Depends on

#201, #200

Part of #198

opened_issues.title: Knowledge library as the document container, with data migration
opened_issues.author: criew
opened_issues.body:
## Context

Documents currently have **no** owning container at all: `io.opaa.indexing.Document` has no workspace
reference and the Liquibase changelogs contain no such column. The permission anchor is not being
moved here, it is being introduced for the first time.

See [`docs/features/spaces-and-assets.md`](docs/features/spaces-and-assets.md) and [ADR-0008](docs/decisions/0008-space-and-asset-model.md).

## Scope

- `KnowledgeLibrary` as the first asset type: id, name, description, owner (user or group),
  organization, `visibility`, `listed`
- `Document.libraryId` and `library_id` on the chunk metadata
- Personal knowledge library "My documents" created together with the personal space
- Library CRUD API and a documents endpoint at `/api/v1/libraries/{id}/documents`
- Upload targets a library, not a space
- **The relational database is the leading store**; the vector store is derived. Documented here and
  in the specification, because it determines how backups are set up

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every document belongs to exactly one knowledge library; the column is non-nullable
- [ ] Every chunk carries `library_id` and `organization_id`
- [ ] Existing documents are migrated into a system library **readable by system admins only**
- [ ] Creating a user creates personal space and personal library atomically
- [ ] Re-indexing keeps the library assignment
- [ ] **Dry run with volume figures** before the `library_id` backfill; migration is resumable and
      the rollback order is documented
- [ ] Backend format, build and test pass

## Depends on

#199, #200 (for group-owned libraries)

Part of #198

opened_issues.title: Introduce groups as permission subjects
opened_issues.author: criew
opened_issues.body:
## Context

Permission entries reference a **user or a group**. Groups are not a convenience feature: the
distribution level "department" is a grant to the department group, and there is deliberately no
department object. Without groups that level does not exist. Groups can also **own an asset**, which
is what keeps centrally maintained libraries alive across staff changes.

See [`docs/features/spaces-and-assets.md`](docs/features/spaces-and-assets.md) and [ADR-0008](docs/decisions/0008-space-and-asset-model.md).

## Scope

- `Group` entity scoped to an organization, with members
- `Group.kind`: `ORG_UNIT` (from the directory, carries a parent unit, can have curators) and
  `AD_HOC` (created in the system, no curator, no distribution level)
- Group management API and admin UI (create, rename, delete, add and remove members)
- A permission subject abstraction resolving to user or group
- Group membership resolution with caching and invalidation on change

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A group can be created, renamed, deleted and have members added and removed
- [ ] Groups never cross an organization boundary
- [ ] Resolving the groups of a user is cached and invalidated immediately on membership change
- [ ] Deleting a group that owns assets is blocked until ownership is transferred
- [ ] Membership is **not** inherited downward: a grant to "Amt 5" reaches exactly the people the
      directory places in that group — no inheritance is invented
- [ ] Backend and frontend format, lint, build and test pass

## Notes

Directory synchronisation is #237 and changes only the origin of memberships, not the permission
model. Responsibility, unlike membership, **is** inherited upward — see #208.

Part of #198

opened_issues.title: Rename workspace to space, add organization scope and reshape space roles
opened_issues.author: criew
opened_issues.body:
## Context

First step of the space and asset model. Mechanical rename plus two semantic changes that must
happen before anything else is built on top, otherwise every later change has to be made twice.

See [`docs/features/spaces-and-assets.md`](docs/features/spaces-and-assets.md) and [ADR-0008](docs/decisions/0008-space-and-asset-model.md).

## Scope

- Rename `Workspace` to `Space` across entity, table, repository, service and controller
- Rename `WorkspaceMembership` to `SpaceMembership`
- `Space.kind`: `PERSONAL` | `PROJECT` | `TEAM`
- `Space.visibility`: `PRIVATE` | `DISCOVERABLE` | `OPEN`
- Replace `WorkspaceRole` with `SpaceRole`: `MEMBER` | `CURATOR` | `ADMIN`
  (`VIEWER`->`MEMBER`, `EDITOR`->`CURATOR`, `ADMIN`->`ADMIN`, `OWNER`->`ADMIN`)
- Keep `ownerId` as an attribute; only the owner or a system admin may delete a space or transfer
  responsibility
- Add `organization_id` to space, membership and user; enforce that nothing crosses an organization
  boundary, including for system admins. Exactly one organization is seeded
- Drop global name uniqueness (`existsByNameIgnoreCase`)
- Users may create `PROJECT` spaces; `TEAM` spaces stay system-admin only
- OpenAPI spec: `/api/v1/workspaces/**` becomes `/api/v1/spaces/**`
- **Remove `/api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/documents`** — declared in the spec with no controller
  implementation and no successor at space level
- Update `typeMappings` / `importMappings` / the `doLast` cleanup block for the renamed enums
- Frontend: `workspaceStore` -> `spaceStore`, `WorkspacePage`, `WorkspaceManagementPage`,
  `CreateWorkspaceDialog`, `Sidebar`, `App`, `services/api.ts`, MSW fixtures and handlers

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Liquibase changelog migrates existing rows with the role mapping above, no data loss
- [ ] The migration is **resumable**; an abort mid-run leaves no inconsistent state
- [ ] A **dry run with volume figures** against a copy of the production data set exists
- [ ] The **rollback order** is documented
- [ ] `ensurePersonalWorkspace` becomes `ensurePersonalSpace` and no longer bypasses validation
- [ ] Two users can each own a project space with the same name
- [ ] A request crossing an organization boundary is rejected, also for system admins
- [ ] No DTO is hand-written; all come from the OpenAPI spec (ADR-0006)
- [ ] No occurrence of `Workspace` remains in backend or frontend production code
- [ ] Backend and frontend format, lint, build and test pass

## Notes

Hard cut without a compatibility layer. Pre-1.0, no external clients. A migration abort is not
security-critical because no permission anchor exists today — the prior state was not more
restrictive.

Part of #198

opened_issues.title: Epic: Space and asset model — replace the workspace model
opened_issues.author: criew
opened_issues.body:
Replace the workspace model with a space and asset model.

## Why

The current workspace is three things at once: document container, permission boundary and
organizing frame. That combination blocks the core product promise — that AI capability becomes
*distributable*.

Worse, the permission anchor does not exist in the implementation at all: `io.opaa.indexing.Document`
has no workspace reference, no Liquibase changelog defines one, and `QueryService` performs a
similarity search **with no filter whatsoever**. This epic introduces the permission-aware search
for the first time rather than moving it.

## The model

> **What is created in a space belongs to the space. What is associated with it keeps its owner.**

- **Assets** (knowledge libraries, agents, prompt libraries) are standalone objects with their own
  owner and ACL. Associating one with a space grants **nothing** — it is pure curation.
- **Space-owned content** (chats, artifacts) lives in exactly one space. It is created as a
  **draft belonging to its author** and becomes visible to all members when the author **places it**
  in the space.

Full specification: [`docs/features/spaces-and-assets.md`](docs/features/spaces-and-assets.md)
Decision, alternatives and surveyed systems: [ADR-0008](docs/decisions/0008-space-and-asset-model.md)

## Ordering — cut by introducibility, not by model logic

Six stakeholder reviews (case worker, unit head, AI champion, operations, sceptic, staff council)
led to a recut. Two independent voices drove it: the AI champion needs *build an agent, share it,
find it in the catalog* early or he stays the bottleneck the model was meant to remove; the sceptic
pointed out that the governance controls a works council agreement depends on were scheduled last,
although the specification itself says no rollout begins without one.

The result is four stages. **Stage A is the only one that is technically mandatory in its order** —
the rest follows what an authority can actually introduce.

### Stage A — Foundation and provability

Nothing is real before this. The permission anchor is introduced here for the first time.

| # | Item | Why here |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | #199 Rename to space, organization scope, three space roles | Mechanical plus two semantic changes; every later change would otherwise be made twice |
| 2 | #200 Groups as permission subjects | Before any grant exists — retrofitting a subject type touches every grant, query and cache |
| 3 | #237 Directory synchronisation as a rights event | The only place where rights change in bulk without a human decision. Gates the **first productive directory connection**, not a pilot: a pilot with manually maintained groups can start before it |
| 4 | #201 Knowledge library as document container, with migration | The first asset type and the only one the vector search depends on |
| 5 | #202 Asset permissions and permission-aware vector search | **The linchpin.** The central gap of the current implementation |
| 6 | #238 Historisation of rights and group memberships | The auditor's question is the *negative* one — an event log cannot answer it. Must be built with the grants, not bolted on |
| 7 | #239 Audit governance: no person-based evaluation path | The audit log is written from step 5 onwards. A switchable statistic does not protect while the same data accrues in the log regardless |

### Stage B — First visible benefit

The path *build an agent, share it, find it*. Note that no space-owned content exists yet in this
stage, so the derivation leak has not been opened — which makes this a safe place to stop and pilot.

| # | Item |
|---|---|
| 8 | #203 Space-asset association as pure curation |
| 9 | #207 Connector sources target exactly one library |
| 10 | #208 Curator roles bound to organizational units |
| 11 | #209 Agent and prompt library assets with the share chain |
| 12 | #210 Asset parameters — **same release as 11**, derivatives created in the meantime cannot be collected back in |
| 13 | #215 Asset catalog: visibility, listed flag, space directory |
| 14 | #240 Succession instead of blocking: assets of departed owners |

### Stage C — Collaboration in the space

| # | Item |
|---|---|
| 15 | #205 Persistent chats with the placement model |
| 16 | #204 Strict mode for spaces (provenance tracking moved into #205, which needs it for the placement dialog) |
| 17 | #206 Artifacts with lifecycle |
| 18 | #216 Retention and governance controls for space-owned content |

### Stage D — Operating and maintaining

| # | Item |
|---|---|
| 19 | #211 Asset versioning with immediate propagation and rollback |
| 20 | #212 Recall by deactivation |
| 21 | #213 Derivatives with permanent provenance |
| 22 | #214 Built-in assets as a distinct origin type |
| 23 | #241 Time limits and recertification of individual grants |
| 24 | #242 Consistency check between vector store and database |

### Deferred until there is evidence

| # | Item |
|---|---|
| 25 | #243 Drift protection for derivatives: deadlines and automatic deactivation |

The most complex behaviour in the model and the only place where an asset changes state without
action by its owner. It presupposes that derivatives arise in relevant numbers — which #210 is meant
to prevent. Build it when the first real case exists.

## Migration

- Personal workspaces become personal spaces; each user additionally gets a personal knowledge
  library
- Shared workspaces become team spaces; roles map `VIEWER`→`MEMBER`, `EDITOR`→`CURATOR`,
  `ADMIN`→`ADMIN`, `OWNER`→`ADMIN`
- Existing documents have **no** workspace assignment today and move into a system library readable
  by system admins only
- `/api/v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/documents` is spec fiction — declared with no controller
  implementation — and is removed without replacement
- Migration must be resumable and preceded by a dry run with volume figures
- Hard cut, no compatibility layer: pre-1.0, no external clients

## Out of scope

Approval and review workflow, agent test bench, the model policy engine itself, SCIM directory
provisioning beyond the group sync in #237, and document versioning.

## Constraints

- DTOs come from the OpenAPI spec only (ADR-0006)
- Library and plugin versions only in `backend/gradle/libs.versions.toml`
- Pre-push checklist applies to every child issue that touches code

---

## Child issues

- [x] #199
- [ ] #200
- [ ] #237

- [ ] #202
- [ ] #238
- [ ] #239

**Stage B — First visible benefit**

- [ ] #203

**Stage C — Collaboration in the space**

- [ ] #205

**Stage D — Operating and maintaining**

opened_issues.title: ci: publish backend and frontend Docker images to GHCR
opened_issues.author: criew
opened_issues.body:
To deploy OPAA without building from source on the target host, CI should publish container images.

Add a workflow that builds `backend/Dockerfile` and `frontend/Dockerfile` on every push to `main` (plus manual dispatch) and pushes them to GHCR as `ghcr.io/criew/opaa-backend` and `ghcr.io/criew/opaa-frontend`, tagged with both `main` and the commit SHA.

This enables a deployment target to run `docker compose pull && docker compose up -d` against a pinned or floating tag instead of checking out the repository.

opened_issues.title: docs: document git worktree usage for parallel agent sessions
opened_issues.author: criew
